variants: Basic, Standard and Customized on the product page. The Basic and Standard columns list 23 degrees of freedom, and the Customized column lists 31 with grippers and 41 with dexterous hands. Booster sells the K1 and T2 on product pages of their own, which this record does not cover.
availability_note: Booster's product page carries Buy Now buttons that open an inquiry form on its store page, which says "Booster Robotics will contact you" and gives a sales email address. The product page states no price and no order path.

hardware.compute: An NVIDIA AGX Orin GPU rated at "200 TOPS AI performance" in every configuration, and an Intel i7 1370p CPU listed for the Standard and Customized configurations.
hardware.sensors: A depth camera, a 9-axis IMU, and a circular 6-microphone array with a speaker. Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.2 are listed as supported.
hardware.actuation: 23 degrees of freedom in the Basic and Standard configurations, 6 per leg, 1 at the waist, 4 per arm (extensible) and 2 in the head, with a maximum peak torque of 130 N·m and dual joint encoders. The page states a size of 118 x 47 x 23 cm and a weight of about 30 kg.
hardware.power: A 10.5 Ah battery, with about 2 hours of walking and about 4 hours of standing listed for the battery life.

developer_access: Booster's developer guide documents a Python SDK for "connecting to real or virtual K1/T1 robots to read data and send control commands" and a C++ SDK "covering both high-level RPC and low-level DDS interfaces". Its booster_deploy repository says it "supports running control policies on Booster robots (sim2real) and MuJoCo (sim2sim)", with TorchScript and ONNX checkpoints chosen by file suffix and a T1 robot configuration. Its booster_train repository documents training reinforcement-learning tasks with "support for the T2, T1, and K1 platforms" and exporting the trained policy "for deployment on real robots", and its booster_gym repository documents training a T1 locomotion policy and deploying it to the physical robot. The product page lists secondary development as supported.
terms_note: Booster's SDK repository says it is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0, and its LICENSE file carries the Apache licence notice rather than the full licence text. Booster's Service Terms & Policies page is a use policy for the robot product: it prohibits private disassembly or modification, restricts use of "the functions and services of this product" for weapons and export-controlled purposes, and says using the product is acceptance of the page, so it is recorded as software terms. It is not a sale contract, and no terms of sale were found at review time. The product page lists a one-year warranty.
not_verified: The documented policy interfaces are Booster's own claims; the Atlas has not verified them. Every source is a Booster web page or a file in a repository Booster can change at any time.
